meta.title: 第2套 · 仔细阅读 A

paragraphs.text: Having a rival can keep you committed to achieving your goals and enhance your overall performance. But before you go out and find an entrepreneur to outcompete, it's important to understand and avoid the traps that often come with rivalry. After all, competitive rivalry can also hinder effective decision-making and increase your willingness to take risks, behaviors that can ultimately hurt your venture's success.

sentences.text: Having a rival can keep you committed to achieving your goals and enhance your overall performance.

analysis.senseInContext: 竞争对手（having a rival 有对手）
examples: The company is a rival to ours. 这家公司是我们的竞争对手。

more.roots: 源自拉丁 rivus（河）→ 共用一条河的人 → 竞争者
more.confusables: rival 名词/动词“与……匹敌”；rivalry 名词“竞争关系”

analysis.senseInContext: 提升、增强（enhance your overall performance 提升整体表现）
examples: Practice enhances confidence. 练习能增强自信。

more.confusables: enhance 偏“提升品质/价值”；increase 偏“数量增加”

analysis.translationLiteral: 有一个竞争对手能让你致力于实现目标，并提升你的整体表现。
analysis.translationNatural: 有个竞争对手，能让你更专注于目标，整体表现也会更好。
analysis.structMarkup: 【Having a rival】 _can keep_ ~you~ ~committed to achieving your goals~ and _enhance_ ~your overall performance~.
analysis.structureSummary: 动名词短语作主语 + 两个并列谓语（keep sb. + 过去分词 / enhance + 宾语）

components.note: 动名词短语作主语，谓语用单数
keep sb. + 形容词/过去分词，表“使某人保持某状态”

components.part: you committed to achieving your goals
components.note: committed to 中 to 是介词，后接动名词

clauses: 本句是简单句，没有从句。
and 连接两个并列谓语：can keep 和 (can) enhance。
be committed to doing sth. 中 to 是介词，后接动名词 achieving。

phrases.usage: to 是介词，后接名词或动名词；不要误用动词原形。
phrases.example: She is committed to improving her English. 她致力于提高英语水平。

phrases.text: keep sb. + 形容词/过去分词
phrases.usage: keep sb. motivated / keep sb. informed。
phrases.example: Goals keep us focused. 目标让我们保持专注。

pitfalls: be committed to doing：to 是介词，不能接动词原形。
动名词短语作主语，谓语用单数 can keep。
enhance 前省略了 can，与 keep 并列。
analysis.paragraphRole: 开篇给出正面观点：竞争对手有益，为下文转折（也有代价）做铺垫。

sentences.text: But before you go out and find an entrepreneur to outcompete, it's important to understand and avoid the traps that often come with rivalry.

analysis.translationLiteral: 但在你出去找一个创业者去超越之前，理解并避免竞争中常见的陷阱很重要。
analysis.translationNatural: 但在你急着找个同行去超越之前，先弄清“竞争”常带来的坑、并避开它们，才是要紧事。
analysis.structMarkup: {But before you go out and find an entrepreneur (to outcompete)}, 【it】 _'s_ ~important (to understand and avoid the traps {that often come with rivalry})~.
analysis.structureSummary: 时间状语从句 + 形式主语句（it is important to do）

components.part: before you go out and find an entrepreneur to outcompete

components.note: 真正主语是后面的不定式

components.part: to understand and avoid the traps that often come with rivalry
components.note: 不定式短语，内含定语从句

clauses: before 引导时间状语从句，“在……之前”。
that often come with rivalry 是定语从句，修饰 the traps。
it is important to do sth. 是形式主语句型。

phrases.usage: go out 在此不表“外出娱乐”，而是“行动起来”。
phrases.example: Go out and find customers. 出去找客户。

phrases.usage: 指出某事物的附带问题或特点。
phrases.example: Fame comes with pressure. 名气伴随压力而来。

pitfalls: before 从句用一般现在时表将来（go, find）。
it 是形式主语，真正主语是不定式 to understand and avoid。
to outcompete 是不定式作后置定语，修饰 entrepreneur。
analysis.paragraphRole: 转折提醒：竞争有陷阱，引出全文要讲的“坑”。

sentences.text: After all, competitive rivalry can also hinder effective decision-making and increase your willingness to take risks, behaviors that can ultimately hurt your venture's success.

analysis.senseInContext: 妨碍、阻碍（hinder effective decision-making 妨碍有效决策）
examples: Bad weather hindered the rescue. 恶劣天气妨碍了救援。

more.confusables: hinder 后可直接接宾语，也可 hinder sb. from doing

analysis.translationLiteral: 毕竟，竞争性对抗也可能妨碍有效决策，并增加你承担风险的意愿，这些行为最终可能损害你的事业成功。
analysis.translationNatural: 毕竟，竞争关系也会干扰你做出有效决策，还会让你更愿意冒风险——而这些最终都可能伤害你的事业。
analysis.structMarkup: (After all), 【competitive rivalry】 _can also hinder_ ~effective decision-making~ and _increase_ ~your willingness to take risks~, ~behaviors {that can ultimately hurt your venture's success}~.
analysis.structureSummary: 主谓宾并列（两个谓语）+ 逗号后的同位语（带定语从句）

components.note: 有效决策（动名词复合名词）
willingness to do 表“……的意愿”

components.part: behaviors that can ultimately hurt your venture's success

clauses: 两个并列谓语：can hinder 与 (can) increase，共用主语 competitive rivalry。
behaviors 是同位语，概括前面提到的两种行为。
that can ultimately hurt your venture's success 是定语从句，修饰 behaviors。

phrases.usage: 及物动词，直接接宾语；同义 block / hamper。
phrases.example: Noise hinders concentration. 噪音妨碍集中注意力。

phrases.usage: 形容词 willing + 名词后缀 -ness；反义 unwillingness。
phrases.example: His willingness to learn impressed us. 他愿意学习，给我们留下深刻印象。

phrases.usage: 复合名词，中间带连字符。
phrases.example: Data improves decision-making. 数据能改善决策。

pitfalls: 两个谓语并列，increase 前省略了 can。
behaviors 是同位语（复数），指代前两种行为，不是新句子主语。
venture's success 中 venture 指“创业项目/事业”。
analysis.paragraphRole: 点出竞争的两个负面作用：妨碍决策、放大冒险倾向。

paragraphs.text: Finding someone you're committed to outcompeting can be a great way to stay focused on your goals and push your venture to the next level. But when you're intently focused on outperforming your rivals, you may begin to develop a "win-at-all-costs" mentality that causes you to ignore how you achieve success. One group of researchers, for example, examined the link between rivalry and unethical behavior. They found that when people compete against their rivals, they are more willing to behave unethically to win. But such behavior may stain your reputation and strain relationships important to your success. One way to avoid this trap is to stop and reflect on what's important. While outperforming your rivals may provide short-term benefits, the loss of your integrity will have long-term consequences.

sentences.text: Finding someone you're committed to outcompeting can be a great way to stay focused on your goals and push your venture to the next level.

analysis.senseInContext: 创业项目、事业（hurt your venture's success 损害你的事业）
examples: The venture failed within a year. 这个创业项目一年内就失败了。

more.confusables: venture 名词“事业/风险项目”；动词“冒险做”（venture to do）

analysis.translationLiteral: 找到一个你决心要超越的人，可以成为保持专注于目标并把事业推向新高度的好方法。
analysis.translationNatural: 找一个你下决心要超越的人，是让自己专注目标、把事业推上一个台阶的好办法。
analysis.structMarkup: 【Finding someone (you're committed to outcompeting)】 _can be_ ~a great way (to stay focused on your goals) and (to push your venture to the next level)~.
analysis.structureSummary: 动名词短语作主语 + 主系表 + 两个并列不定式作后置定语

components.part: Finding someone you're committed to outcompeting
components.note: 动名词短语作主语，内含省略关系词的定语从句

components.part: to stay focused on your goals and to push your venture to the next level
components.note: 两个并列不定式，说明 way 的内容

clauses: you're committed to outcompeting 是省略关系词的定语从句，修饰 someone。
be committed to doing 的 to 是介词，故用 outcompeting。

phrases.usage: stay + 过去分词作表语；也可 remain focused on。
phrases.example: Stay focused on one task at a time. 一次专注一件事。

phrases.text: take/push sth. to the next level
phrases.usage: 口语高频搭配。
phrases.example: Practice can take your skills to the next level. 练习能让你的技能更上一层。

pitfalls: you're committed to outcompeting：to 是介词，用动名词。
不定式并列时第二个 to 可省略，但保留更清楚。
动名词短语作主语，谓语用单数 can be。
analysis.paragraphRole: 重申竞争的正面价值，与上一段“陷阱”形成对照，推动辩证论述。

sentences.text: But when you're intently focused on outperforming your rivals, you may begin to develop a "win-at-all-costs" mentality that causes you to ignore how you achieve success.

analysis.senseInContext: 心态、思维方式（a "win-at-all-costs" mentality 不惜代价求胜的心态）
examples: He has a winner's mentality. 他有赢家的心态。

more.confusables: mentality 偏“群体/固定心态”；mindset 更中性

analysis.translationLiteral: 但当你专注地想要胜出对手时，你可能开始形成一种“不惜一切代价求胜”的心态，这种心态让你忽略自己是如何取得成功的。
analysis.translationNatural: 可当你一门心思想赢过对手时，可能就会生出“不择手段也要赢”的心态，从而不再在意成功是怎么来的。
analysis.structMarkup: {But when you're intently focused on outperforming your rivals}, 【you】 _may begin to develop_ ~a "win-at-all-costs" mentality~ {that causes you to ignore how you achieve success}.
analysis.structureSummary: 时间状语从句 + 主谓宾 + 定语从句（内含宾语从句）

components.part: when you're intently focused on outperforming your rivals
that causes you to ignore how you achieve success

clauses: when 引导时间状语从句。
that causes you to ignore... 是定语从句，修饰 mentality。
how you achieve success 是 how 引导的宾语从句，作 ignore 的宾语。

phrases.usage: focus on 后接名词/动名词；intently 修饰程度。
phrases.example: She is focused on finishing the report. 她专注于完成报告。

phrases.usage: 固定短语；win-at-all-costs 作复合形容词。
phrases.example: He wanted to win at all costs. 他想不惜一切代价赢。

pitfalls: win-at-all-costs 是复合形容词，整体修饰 mentality。
ignore 后接 how 从句，用陈述语序。
outperform = out-（超过）+ perform。
analysis.paragraphRole: 指出竞争的风险一：为了赢而失去底线，引出下文的“不道德行为”。

sentences.text: One group of researchers, for example, examined the link between rivalry and unethical behavior.

analysis.translationLiteral: 例如，一组研究人员考察了竞争对抗与不道德行为之间的联系。
analysis.translationNatural: 比如，有一组研究者就研究了“竞争关系”与“不道德行为”之间的关联。
analysis.structMarkup: (One group of researchers), (for example), _examined_ 【the link (between rivalry and unethical behavior)】.
analysis.structureSummary: 主谓宾结构 + 插入语 + 后置定语

components.part: the link between rivalry and unethical behavior
components.note: between...and... 作后置定语修饰 link

clauses: 本句是简单句，没有从句。
between rivalry and unethical behavior 是介词短语作后置定语，修饰 the link。

phrases.text: the link between A and B
phrases.meaning: A 与 B 之间的联系
phrases.usage: link 常与 between...and... 搭配；同义 the connection between。
phrases.example: Studies show a link between sleep and memory. 研究显示睡眠与记忆有关联。

phrases.usage: un-（否定）+ ethical（道德的）；名词 ethics 伦理学。
phrases.example: The company punished unethical behavior. 公司惩处了不道德行为。

pitfalls: link 与 between...and... 固定搭配，不用 link of。
unethical 是“不道德的”，不是“不伦理的学科”。
analysis.paragraphRole: 引入研究证据，把“不择手段”的心态落到实证上。

sentences.text: They found that when people compete against their rivals, they are more willing to behave unethically to win.

analysis.translationLiteral: 他们发现，当人们与竞争对手竞争时，他们更愿意为了获胜而做出不道德的行为。
analysis.translationNatural: 他们发现：人和对手竞争时，为了赢，会更愿意做不道德的事。
analysis.structMarkup: 【They】 _found_ ~{that when people compete against their rivals, they are more willing to behave unethically to win}~.
analysis.structureSummary: 主谓 + 宾语从句（从句内含时间状语从句）

components.part: when people compete against their rivals
they are more willing to behave unethically to win
components.note: be willing to do 表意愿

clauses: that 引导宾语从句，作 found 的宾语。
从句内部 when 引导时间状语从句。
be willing to do sth. 表示“愿意做某事”。

phrases.usage: 也可 compete with（竞争/抗衡）；against 更强调对抗。
phrases.example: They compete against each other for the prize. 他们为奖品互相竞争。

phrases.usage: 反义 be unwilling/reluctant to do。
phrases.example: He is willing to help. 他愿意帮忙。

pitfalls: compete against/with：against 强调对抗关系。
behave unethically 中 unethically 是副词修饰 behave。
to win 是不定式作目的状语。
analysis.paragraphRole: 给出研究结论：竞争会降低道德底线。

sentences.text: But such behavior may stain your reputation and strain relationships important to your success.

analysis.translationLiteral: 但这种行为可能玷污你的名声，并让你成功所必需的关系变得紧张。
analysis.translationNatural: 可这种行为会弄脏你的名声，也会让对你成功很关键的人际关系变得紧张。
analysis.structMarkup: {But} 【such behavior】 _may stain_ ~your reputation~ and _strain_ ~relationships (important to your success)~.
analysis.structureSummary: 主谓宾并列（两个谓语）+ 后置定语
clauses: 本句是简单句，没有从句。
and 连接两个并列谓语：may stain 与 (may) strain。
important to your success 是形容词短语作后置定语，修饰 relationships。

phrases.usage: stain 本义“弄脏”，引申为“玷污”；同义 damage one's reputation。
phrases.example: The scandal stained his reputation. 丑闻玷污了他的名声。

phrases.usage: strain 作动词表“使紧张、拉紧”。
phrases.example: Long hours can strain family relationships. 长时间工作会让家庭关系紧张。

pitfalls: strain 在此是动词“使紧张”，不是名词“压力”。
important to your success 后置修饰 relationships，不是表语。
第二个谓语 strain 前省略了 may。
analysis.paragraphRole: 说明不道德行为的代价：名声与人脉双损。

sentences.text: One way to avoid this trap is to stop and reflect on what's important.

analysis.translationLiteral: 避免这个陷阱的一个方法是停下来反思什么才是重要的。
analysis.translationNatural: 想避开这个坑，一个办法是先停下来，想清楚什么才是真正重要的。
analysis.structMarkup: 【One way (to avoid this trap)】 _is_ ~to stop and reflect on what's important~.
analysis.structureSummary: 主系表结构：主语带不定式后置定语，表语是不定式短语

components.part: to stop and reflect on what's important
components.note: 不定式作表语，内含宾语从句

clauses: what's important 是 what 引导的宾语从句，作 reflect on 的宾语。
不定式 to stop and reflect 作表语，说明“方法是什么”。

phrases.usage: 后接名词或从句；同义 think about carefully。
phrases.example: Take time to reflect on your progress. 花点时间反思你的进展。

phrases.usage: trap 隐喻“圈套、误区”。
phrases.example: Many young writers fall into this trap. 许多年轻作者掉进这个陷阱。

pitfalls: what's important 是宾语从句，不能换成 that's important。
one way to do sth. 中 to do 作后置定语。
stop and reflect：两个动词并列，and 不能省。
analysis.paragraphRole: 给出第一条对策：先停下来反思。

sentences.text: While outperforming your rivals may provide short-term benefits, the loss of your integrity will have long-term consequences.

analysis.senseInContext: 诚信、正直（the loss of your integrity 失去诚信）
examples: Academic integrity matters more than grades. 学术诚信比成绩更重要。

more.roots: in-（不）+ teg（触碰）+ -rity → 未被触碰 → 完整、正直
more.confusables: integrity 不可数，表“诚信/完整性”；integrate 是动词“整合”

analysis.translationLiteral: 尽管胜出对手可能带来短期好处，但失去诚信会有长期后果。
analysis.translationNatural: 赢过对手可能带来短期好处，可一旦丢了诚信，代价是长期的。
analysis.structMarkup: {While outperforming your rivals may provide short-term benefits}, 【the loss of your integrity】 _will have_ ~long-term consequences~.
analysis.structureSummary: 让步状语从句 + 主谓宾

components.part: While outperforming your rivals may provide short-term benefits

clauses: while 引导让步状语从句，意为“虽然、尽管”。
从句主语是动名词短语 outperforming your rivals。

phrases.usage: 不可数名词；常搭 personal/professional integrity。
phrases.example: She is known for her integrity. 她以正直著称。

phrases.usage: 反义 short-term benefits（短期好处），常成对出现。
phrases.example: Short-term gains can bring long-term consequences. 短期收益可能带来长期后果。

pitfalls: while 在此是“虽然”（让步），不是“当……时”。
integrity 不可数，不说 an integrity。
short-term / long-term 作定语时带连字符。
analysis.paragraphRole: 总结本段：短期收益 vs 长期代价，给出价值判断。

paragraphs.text: One reason having a rival can enhance your venture's performance is that it creates a level of excitement that drives you to work harder. But this eagerness to win may also hurt your venture's success, particularly when it causes you to make impulsive, insensible decisions. But it's possible to avoid such costly mistakes by making a habit of engaging in critical thinking, such as considering opposing viewpoints and conducting cost-benefit analyses, especially for those decisions that are complex and can determine the future of your venture.

sentences.text: One reason having a rival can enhance your venture's performance is that it creates a level of excitement that drives you to work harder.

analysis.senseInContext: 竞争对手（having a rival 有对手）
examples: The company is a rival to ours. 这家公司是我们的竞争对手。

more.roots: 源自拉丁 rivus（河）→ 共用一条河的人 → 竞争者
more.confusables: rival 名词/动词“与……匹敌”；rivalry 名词“竞争关系”

analysis.senseInContext: 提升、增强（enhance your overall performance 提升整体表现）
examples: Practice enhances confidence. 练习能增强自信。

more.confusables: enhance 偏“提升品质/价值”；increase 偏“数量增加”

analysis.translationLiteral: 拥有对手能提升你事业表现的一个原因是，它会制造一种兴奋感，驱使你更努力地工作。
analysis.translationNatural: 有对手能让你事业更好的原因之一是：它会激起一股兴奋劲，逼着你更拼。
analysis.structMarkup: 【One reason (having a rival can enhance your venture's performance)】 _is_ ~{that it creates a level of excitement (that drives you to work harder)}~.
analysis.structureSummary: 主系表结构：主语带定语从句，表语是 that 从句（内含第二层定语从句）

components.part: having a rival can enhance your venture's performance
that it creates a level of excitement
that drives you to work harder

clauses: having a rival can enhance... 是省略关系词的定语从句，修饰 one reason（= the reason why...）。
that it creates a level of excitement 是表语从句。
that drives you to work harder 是定语从句，修饰 excitement。

phrases.usage: drive 在此为“驱使”；drive sb. crazy 是“把某人逼疯”。
phrases.example: Curiosity drives scientists to explore. 好奇心驱使科学家探索。

phrases.usage: a level of + 名词 表示“某种程度的”。
phrases.example: The race creates a level of excitement. 比赛带来一种兴奋感。

pitfalls: one reason 后的定语从句常省略关系词，别把 having 当主句主语。
两个 that：第一个引导表语从句，第二个引导定语从句。
drive sb. to do 中 to 不能省。
analysis.paragraphRole: 解释竞争的正面机制：兴奋感驱动更努力。

sentences.text: But this eagerness to win may also hurt your venture's success, particularly when it causes you to make impulsive, insensible decisions.

analysis.senseInContext: 急切、渴望（this eagerness to win 这种求胜的急切）
examples: Her eagerness to learn impressed us. 她求学的热切让我们印象深刻。

more.confusables: eager to do（形容词）；eagerness to do（名词）

analysis.senseInContext: 冲动的（impulsive decisions 冲动的决定）
examples: He is impulsive and often regrets it. 他很冲动，常常后悔。

more.roots: im-（向内）+ puls（推）+ -ive → 被推着走
more.confusables: impulsive 带贬义；spontaneous 表“自发的”（中性）

analysis.translationLiteral: 但这种想赢的急切也可能损害你的事业成功，特别是当它导致你做出冲动的、不明智的决定时。
analysis.translationNatural: 可这种急于求胜，也可能反噬你的事业，尤其是当你因此做出冲动、欠考虑的决定时。
analysis.structMarkup: {But} 【this eagerness to win】 _may also hurt_ ~your venture's success~, (particularly when it causes you to make impulsive, insensible decisions).
analysis.structureSummary: 主谓宾 + 时间状语从句（when 引导）

components.note: eagerness to do 表“……的急切”

components.part: particularly when it causes you to make impulsive, insensible decisions
components.note: when 引导，particularly 加强语气

clauses: when 引导时间状语从句。
cause sb. to do sth. 是使役结构。

phrases.usage: eager（形容词）+ -ness；be eager to do。
phrases.example: His eagerness to please surprised us. 他那种急于讨好的样子让我们意外。

phrases.usage: impulsive 带贬义；impulse 是名词“冲动”。
phrases.example: Avoid impulsive purchases. 避免冲动消费。

pitfalls: insensible 在此意为“不明智的、无感觉的”，与 insensible to（对……无感觉）不同。
when 从句用一般现在时表将来。
cause sb. to make：to 不能省。
analysis.paragraphRole: 指出竞争风险的第二种表现：冲动决策。

sentences.text: But it's possible to avoid such costly mistakes by making a habit of engaging in critical thinking, such as considering opposing viewpoints and conducting cost-benefit analyses, especially for those decisions that are complex and can determine the future of your venture.

analysis.senseInContext: 创业项目、事业（hurt your venture's success 损害你的事业）
examples: The venture failed within a year. 这个创业项目一年内就失败了。

more.confusables: venture 名词“事业/风险项目”；动词“冒险做”（venture to do）

analysis.translationLiteral: 但通过养成批判性思考的习惯——例如考虑对立观点、进行成本收益分析——是有可能避免这类代价高昂的错误的，尤其是对那些复杂且能决定你事业未来的决策。
analysis.translationNatural: 但只要养成批判性思考的习惯，这类代价惨重的错误是可以避免的——比如主动考虑反面观点、做成本收益分析，尤其是对那些复杂且关乎事业前途的决定。
analysis.structMarkup: {But} 【it】 _'s_ ~possible (to avoid such costly mistakes)~ (by making a habit of engaging in critical thinking), (such as considering opposing viewpoints and conducting cost-benefit analyses), (especially for those decisions {that are complex and can determine the future of your venture}).
analysis.structureSummary: 形式主语句 + 方式状语 + 举例 + 范围状语（内含定语从句）

components.part: by making a habit of engaging in critical thinking
such as considering opposing viewpoints and conducting cost-benefit analyses
components.note: such as 后接两个并列动名词

components.part: especially for those decisions that are complex and can determine the future of your venture

clauses: it is possible to do sth. 是形式主语句型。
by making a habit of doing sth. 表示手段。
that are complex and can determine the future of your venture 是定语从句，修饰 those decisions。

phrases.text: make a habit of doing sth.
phrases.usage: habit 前用 a；也可 get into the habit of。
phrases.example: Make a habit of reviewing notes daily. 养成每天复习笔记的习惯。

phrases.usage: engage in 后接名词/动名词。
phrases.example: Students should engage in critical thinking. 学生应进行批判性思考。

phrases.usage: 复合名词，复数 analyses（analysis 的复数）。
phrases.example: Run a cost-benefit analysis before investing. 投资前做成本收益分析。

pitfalls: by making 中 by + 动名词表手段，不能用 to make。
such as 后接动名词，与前面 make a habit of 的结构保持一致。
analyses 是 analysis 的复数，注意拼写。
analysis.paragraphRole: 给出第一条实质对策：用批判性思考对冲冲动决策。

paragraphs.text: The sense of eagerness that comes with having a rival can not only cause you to make poorer decisions, but it can also lead you to take greater risks that put your venture in peril. One way you can overcome the risk-inducing effects of rivalry that stand to endanger your venture's success is to remain attentive to your emotional state and actively monitor how such feelings are affecting your decision-making.

sentences.text: The sense of eagerness that comes with having a rival can not only cause you to make poorer decisions, but it can also lead you to take greater risks that put your venture in peril.

analysis.senseInContext: 急切、渴望（this eagerness to win 这种求胜的急切）
examples: Her eagerness to learn impressed us. 她求学的热切让我们印象深刻。

more.confusables: eager to do（形容词）；eagerness to do（名词）

analysis.senseInContext: 竞争对手（having a rival 有对手）
examples: The company is a rival to ours. 这家公司是我们的竞争对手。

more.roots: 源自拉丁 rivus（河）→ 共用一条河的人 → 竞争者
more.confusables: rival 名词/动词“与……匹敌”；rivalry 名词“竞争关系”

analysis.senseInContext: 创业项目、事业（hurt your venture's success 损害你的事业）
examples: The venture failed within a year. 这个创业项目一年内就失败了。

more.confusables: venture 名词“事业/风险项目”；动词“冒险做”（venture to do）

analysis.senseInContext: 危险（put your venture in peril 置你的事业于险境）
examples: The species is in peril. 该物种处于危险中。

more.confusables: in peril = in danger；peril 更书面、语气更重

analysis.translationLiteral: 拥有对手所带来的急切感不仅可能让你做出更差的决策，还可能让你承担更大风险，从而使你的事业陷入危险。
analysis.translationNatural: 有对手带来的那股急切，不光会让你决策变差，还会推着你冒更大的险，把你的事业置于险境。
analysis.structMarkup: 【The sense of eagerness (that comes with having a rival)】 _can not only cause_ ~you to make poorer decisions~, {but it can also lead you to take greater risks (that put your venture in peril)}.
analysis.structureSummary: not only...but also... 并列两个分句；主语带定语从句，第二分句宾补带定语从句

components.part: that comes with having a rival
can not only cause you to make poorer decisions
but it can also lead you to take greater risks
that put your venture in peril

clauses: not only...but also... 连接两个并列分句，not only 置于句首时第一分句可部分倒装，此处未倒装。
that comes with having a rival 是定语从句，修饰 eagerness。
that put your venture in peril 是定语从句，修饰 risks。
lead sb. to do sth. 表示“导致某人做某事”。

phrases.usage: 连接并列成分；连接分句时注意结构对称。
phrases.example: It not only saves time but also cuts costs. 它不仅省时还降成本。

phrases.usage: peril 比 danger 更书面；同义 endanger。
phrases.example: Reckless spending put the firm in peril. 挥霍无度让公司陷入危险。

pitfalls: not only...but also... 两边结构要对称（cause to do / lead to do）。
that put（复数 risks）不是 that puts。
in peril = 处于危险中。
analysis.paragraphRole: 把风险的后果升级：从“决策差”到“危及事业”。

sentences.text: One way you can overcome the risk-inducing effects of rivalry that stand to endanger your venture's success is to remain attentive to your emotional state and actively monitor how such feelings are affecting your decision-making.

analysis.senseInContext: 留意的、关注的（remain attentive to your emotional state 留意自己的情绪）
examples: Be attentive to your body's signals. 留意身体的信号。

more.roots: at-（向）+ tent（伸展）+ -ive → 注意力伸向
more.confusables: attentive 后接 to；attention 是名词

analysis.senseInContext: 监控、观察（actively monitor how such feelings are affecting 主动观察这些情绪如何影响）
examples: Doctors monitor the patient's heart rate. 医生监测病人的心率。

more.confusables: monitor 动词“监测”；名词指“显示器/监控器”

analysis.translationLiteral: 你可以克服竞争那种可能危及你事业成功的（诱使冒险的）影响的一种方法，是留意自己的情绪状态，并主动监控这些感受如何影响你的决策。
analysis.translationNatural: 竞争会诱使你冒险、甚至危及事业；要克服这种影响，一个办法是留意自己的情绪，主动观察这些情绪怎样左右你的判断。
analysis.structMarkup: 【One way (you can overcome the risk-inducing effects of rivalry {that stand to endanger your venture's success})】 _is_ ~to remain attentive to your emotional state and actively monitor how such feelings are affecting your decision-making~.
analysis.structureSummary: 主系表结构：主语带定语从句与第二层定语从句，表语为两个并列不定式

components.part: you can overcome the risk-inducing effects of rivalry
components.note: 省略 that/in which，修饰 way

components.part: that stand to endanger your venture's success
to remain attentive to your emotional state
and actively monitor how such feelings are affecting your decision-making
components.note: 不定式并列，内含宾语从句

clauses: you can overcome... 是省略关系词的定语从句，修饰 one way（= the way in which you can...）。
that stand to endanger your venture's success 是定语从句，修饰 effects。
how such feelings are affecting your decision-making 是 how 引导的宾语从句，作 monitor 的宾语。
stand to do sth. 表示“很可能导致”。

phrases.usage: 复合形容词：名词 + 现在分词。
phrases.example: Risk-inducing habits are hard to notice. 诱发风险的习气很难察觉。

phrases.usage: 常搭 stand to lose/gain/endanger。
phrases.example: The company stands to lose millions. 公司可能损失数百万。

phrases.usage: attentive to + 名词；同义 pay attention to。
phrases.example: Remain attentive to changes in the market. 要留意市场变化。

pitfalls: one way 后定语从句省略 in which/that，阅读时先跳过定位 is。
两个定语从句接连（effects → that stand to...），辨清修饰对象。
monitor 后接 how 从句，用陈述语序。
analysis.paragraphRole: 给出第二条对策：情绪觉察与自我监控，收束全文。

questions.stem: How can competitive rivalry benefit entrepreneurs according to the passage?

options.text: By enabling them to outcompete other entrepreneurs.
By enabling them to make their venture a success.
By helping them to reach long-term goals.
By helping them to stay goal-oriented.

questions.stem: What is one of the traps entrepreneurs may often fall into when competing with rivals?

options.text: They may adopt strategies that are bound to ruin their venture.
They may resort to unethical means to outperform their rivals.
They may be too eager to succeed while ignoring the huge labor cost.
They may be intently focused on winning at the current market level.

questions.stem: What are entrepreneurs advised to do to avoid traps that often accompany rivalry?

options.text: Deliberate on what really matters.
Prioritize reaping immediate benefits.
Estimate the long-term consequences.
Reflect on what successes are achievable.

questions.stem: How can entrepreneurs avoid making impulsive and insensible decisions?

options.text: By engaging themselves in critical reasoning.
By developing a habit of keeping their integrity.
By criticizing themselves for previous poor performances.
By refraining from being too excited about their successes.

questions.stem: How can entrepreneurs overcome the risk-inducing effects of rivalry?

options.text: By paying close attention to their current performance.
By taking steps that stand to endanger their rivals' success.
By monitoring how their decision-making impacts their mentality.
By keeping their emotions in check to avoid making poor decisions.
